classification.difficultyReason: Students select the converse angle condition that makes the named lines parallel, translate the labelled expressions into an equality or supplementary sum, and solve a simple equation.

content.prompt: In each diagram, find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$ that will make $AB$ parallel to $CD$. Give all reasons.

spec.description: Segments AB and CD with diagonal AD; no parallel marks or angle arcs. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle BAD is 50 degrees; angle ADC is theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 50 degrees and unknown theta are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
Then the alternate angles are equal, so $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: AB above CD, joined by BD; right-angle square at D. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABD is alpha plus 20 degrees; angle BDC is 90 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown expression and right-angle given remain visible.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles must be supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+20^\circ+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha+110^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
Hence $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: A, C and F are collinear; rays AB and CD extend right. No parallel marks or angle arcs. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle BAC is 110 degrees; angle DCF is 2 beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown expression are visible.

answer.worked:
Corresponding angles must be equal:
$$\begin{align*}2\beta&=110^\circ\\\beta&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$
Hence $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Boundary A-B-D-C-A with diagonal AD. No parallel marks or angle arcs. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle BAD is 60 degrees; angle CDA is 3 gamma.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown expression are visible.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles must be equal:
$$\begin{align*}3\gamma&=60^\circ\\\gamma&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
Hence $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABCD and diagonal DB. No parallel marks or angle arcs. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABD is 2 alpha; angle BDC is 40 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown expression are visible.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles must be equal:
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha&=40^\circ\\\alpha&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
Hence $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Trapezium-shaped ABCD with longer base DC; no parallel marks or angle arcs. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle DAB is 100 degrees; angle ADC is alpha plus 30 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown expression are visible.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles must be supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}100^\circ+\alpha+30^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha+130^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
Hence $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Z-shaped AB-BC-CD arrangement. No parallel marks or angle arcs. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABC is 60 degrees; angle BCD is beta plus 10 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown expression are visible.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles must be equal:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+10^\circ&=60^\circ\\\beta&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
Hence $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: AB above CD crossed by an extended rising transversal. No parallel marks or angle arcs. Ordinary source blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: The two right-side co-interior angles are 100 degrees and alpha plus 50 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown expression are visible.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles must be supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}100^\circ+\alpha+50^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha+150^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
Hence $AB\parallel CD$.
